meta.title: MCO · One review, individual provider answers
meta.subtitle: Default parallel review path · CLI or MCP · pinned source 3cfce13 · no synthesis

components.label: Review entry + validation
components.explanation: CLI resolves configuration, prompt, selected providers and scope; MCP validates repo/providers and builds the same invocation inputs in _sync_review (called via asyncio.to_thread). Both normally create one invocation per selected provider, using its configured model. Target paths must stay inside the repository and allowed paths. Read-only is the default permission profile, not a universal MCO sandbox: provider support and overrides matter. The npm wrapper launches the Python CLI; this is not an HTTP review endpoint.

components.label: Invocation scheduler
components.explanation: With chain, debate and synthesis disabled, run_invocation_workflow directly calls run_invocations. It submits each invocation to a ThreadPoolExecutor; max_provider_parallelism caps workers (otherwise one per invocation). Futures are tracked by original input index, so completion order does not reorder final outputs. A global deadline sets the shared stop event and cancels queued futures; workers handle running-provider cancellation.

components.label: Per-invocation worker
components.explanation: _run_one_invocation builds TaskInput with repo, prompt, scope, model, permissions and artifact root, then starts the chosen adapter with a bounded startup deadline. It polls status and reads raw stdout/stderr files, rather than an in-memory stdout pipe. Output changes reset the stall deadline. Provider-specific transport decoding extracts deltas and the final raw answer. Failures, timeouts and cancellation become individual records containing invocation_id, provider, model, status, output, error and exit_code; one failure does not discard another provider's answer.

components.label: Selected provider adapters
components.explanation: The registry maps selected provider IDs to adapter objects (for example ClaudeAdapter and CodexAdapter). ShimAdapterBase builds provider commands, starts subprocesses in the repository directory and redirects stdout/stderr to raw log files. Its poll and cancel methods supervise child processes. Provider adapters own command flags and answer decoding; Codex, for example, translates sandbox/model options and decodes JSON events. CLI can select ACP instead, but that alternative is outside this default-shim view.

components.label: Provider CLI processes
components.explanation: The shim launches installed provider executables (for example codex) with cwd set to the requested repository, configured flags, and prompt arguments. Each selected invocation has its own run handle and raw log files. These executables are outside MCO's Python process. The checkout establishes their launch contract, not their internal model execution, network endpoints, authentication behavior or hosted infrastructure; none is inferred here.

components.label: Individual result envelope
components.explanation: After futures finish, run_invocations counts successful results and returns task_id, stage, status, exit_code, outputs and artifact_root. Each output retains its own provider/model, answer and status; this path neither merges findings nor synthesizes a consensus. CLI --json prints the envelope without each output's stderr, then returns its exit_code; text/JSONL modes can stream answer deltas and completion events. MCP wraps the workflow result in _ok(result).

components.label: Optional saved review files
components.explanation: When CLI result mode is artifact or both (or --save-artifacts promotes stdout to both), answers and run metadata are retained under artifact_base/task_id, normally reports/review/task_id. Workers append per-invocation answer deltas; InvocationArtifactWriter writes run.json and result.md after aggregation. Without persistence, MCO still uses temporary provider logs and answer files, then cleans them up and returns null artifact paths. MCP review does not request persistence. This is a local filesystem, not a database service.

cards.title: One request → N independent answers
items: Shared prompt + validated scope; one default invocation per selected provider.
Bounded parallel execution; final outputs preserve selection order, not completion order.

cards.title: Failure isolation, not consensus
items: Each invocation reports success, failure, timeout or cancellation with its own answer/error.
Aggregate status is complete, partial or failed. No findings schema or automatic synthesis.

cards.title: Scope and evidence limits
items: Default shim path only; opt-in chain, debate, synthesis and ACP are not expanded.
Read-only maps to provider flags; external provider internals and remote services are not established.
